candidate_ref.tested_subclaim: AgentCliBackend canonical AgentIO event append path uses an instance-local threading.Lock and routes project-scoped logging to <project_root>/events.jsonl at the worker-frozen Argus commit.

tested_scope.scope_limit: Only the AgentIO canonical append/routing/lock-granularity subclaim was tested. The broader claim that exactly three and no fourth production events.jsonl append mechanisms exist was not re-audited in this slice. Migration locking, JsonlEventSink locking, Windows behavior, delimiter recovery, rotation, Mission View projection, and future/main-head behavior were not tested.

observations: The exact worker-frozen Argus commit exists and resolves as 2894b434affaff3a28c1fbbcd5c39f2e7a832236.
At that commit, AgentIOLogger.__init__ creates self.io_log_lock = threading.Lock().
AgentIOLogger.log() normalizes/redacts the row and calls _jsonl_append(path, safe_row, self.io_log_lock).
_jsonl_append() enters the supplied lock and appends one JSON line with path.open('a', encoding='utf-8').

At that commit, AgentCliBackend._agent_io_log_path() returns project_root / 'events.jsonl' whenever a project_root usage context exists; otherwise it falls back to ARGUS_SKILL_AGENT_IO_LOG or <working_dir>/.argus/events.jsonl.

assessment.reason: The official source at the exact frozen commit directly supports both the instance-local lock and project-scoped canonical events.jsonl routing portions of worker writer-inventory item 2.
assessment.uncertainty: No runtime test was executed; this is a source-level primary verification of the exact frozen code. A threading.Lock is process-local, so this verification does not establish cross-process serialization.

bounded_effect: Verified one exact primary-source subclaim from the sealed C32 open_source artifact against the worker-frozen upstream commit; no worker state, O state, scheduler, branch, or source repository was mutated.
